title: RAVEN rover and helicopter analog missions
research_objective: Compare rover and aerial field approaches for assessing and sampling volcanic units and overlying sediment.
selection_rationale: The field contains basalt flows of different ages and surface sediments relevant to Mars exploration.
experiment: Separate simulated rover and helicopter field missions with imaging, sampling and geochemistry.
limitations: Vehicle operational limits differ from measured site slope. Icelandic weather and field support affect scheduling.

title: Holuhraun grainflow observations
research_objective: Assess whether wind-fed dry sand grainflows could reproduce some properties of Martian recurring slope lineae.
selection_rationale: Windblown sand banks against a recent lava front, enabling observations of active grainflows.
experiment: Repeat field imaging and interpretation of dry granular flows.
limitations: The Earth observations support a mechanism comparison with different atmosphere and gravity.

title: Icelandic lava-cave UAV survey
research_objective: Evaluate small volcanic caves as candidate analog targets and assess how aerial imaging resolves their entrances.
selection_rationale: Accessible small vent openings in basaltic fissure flows provide a surface-imaging comparison for candidate Martian cave entrances.
experiment: UAV imagery and photogrammetric surface reconstruction.
limitations: Visible openings and surface products provide limited information on deeper cavity geometry.

title: Atacama dry-limit soil study
research_objective: Investigate exceptionally arid soils as an analog for interpreting Viking organic and life-detection results.
selection_rationale: The aridity gradient allowed comparison with exceptionally dry soils near Yungay.
environment: Low detected organics in selected samples
experiment: Field sampling and published laboratory comparison of detection results.
limitations: Results depend on selected soil samples and detection methods.

title: University Valley climate and energy balance
research_objective: Characterize climate, subsurface heat transfer and controls on ground-ice stability for Mars-relevant conditions.
selection_rationale: An upland polar desert preserves dry permafrost over ice-cemented ground.
experiment: Multi-year weather and ground-temperature observations with an energy balance model.
limitations: Results depend on local snow, exposure, and terrestrial atmospheric conditions.

title: Haughton-Mars Project 2005 logistics and operations expedition
research_objective: Assess the research station as a Moon and Mars logistics analog and collect data for supply-chain modeling.
selection_rationale: A rocky high-Arctic impact terrain combines diverse landforms with an isolated operating environment.
experiment: 2005 field expedition testing logistics concepts and technologies for joint human and robotic exploration.
limitations: Earth weather and terrain differ from planetary conditions. Current logistics require separate verification.

title: Cinder Lake Apollo location test
research_objective: Evaluate whether crews can locate themselves on a mapped crater pattern after a simulated lunar landing.
selection_rationale: Cinder-covered ground could be modified to recreate part of a mapped lunar crater pattern.
experiment: Constructed field with a lunar module mock-up and crew localization exercise.
limitations: Engineered geometry, local material and Earth gravity constrain applicability.

title: Desert RATS lunar rover field test
research_objective: Collect engineering and human-factors measurements from unpressurized and pressurized rover concepts during extended mission-like use.
selection_rationale: The broad lava-flow test area supplied realistic surface routes and room for long traverses, night driving and overnight operations.
environment: Rocky routes and a large traverse area
experiment: Field test with prototype rovers, driving, simulated EVA and overnight operations.
limitations: Hardware results reflect the tested prototypes, crew and Earth conditions.

title: JETT3 Artemis field simulation
research_objective: Exercise integrated crew, science, ground support, tools and procedures for Artemis lunar EVAs.
selection_rationale: Remote rocky high-desert volcanic terrain with limited communications infrastructure let the team test geologic sampling and distributed support together.
experiment: Integrated field simulation with astronaut EVAs, geologic sampling and a mission-control science team.
limitations: The S P Mountain point is regional. Earth gravity and atmosphere affect field task performance.

title: USGS S P Mountain volcanic-process field analog
research_objective: Teach field recognition of volcanic landforms and eruption products relevant to other planetary surfaces.
selection_rationale: A compact cinder cone, lava flow and graben allow observers to relate distinctive surface textures and mapped landforms to volcanic processes.
experiment: USGS geologic field guide with mapped stops and documented observations.
limitations: Field guide observations support process comparisons at a regional scale.

title: Lidar survey of Indian Tunnel
research_objective: Assess how lidar characterizes the surface, access pits and interior of a lava tube for planetary exploration.
selection_rationale: A known lava tube with collapse openings and an accessible interior allows comparison between surface observations and surveyed geometry.
experiment: Terrestrial lidar survey combining surface and interior scans.
limitations: The surveyed terrestrial tube does not establish the geometry or accessibility of any off-world cave.

title: NASA BASALT volcanic environments at Mauna Ulu
research_objective: Select basaltic field targets for comparisons of volcanic geology and rock alteration with Mars.
selection_rationale: Young shield lavas and areas of active fumarolic alteration allow comparison of altered and relatively fresh basalt.
experiment: Field target characterization using geologic and remote sensing evidence.
limitations: Terrestrial water, gases and weathering modify the analog setting.

title: Assessment of Ibex dunes as an aeolian Mars analog
research_objective: Characterize dune morphology, migration, sand properties and winds relevant to Martian dunes.
selection_rationale: An active, topographically constrained dune field permits comparison of bedforms, sediment transport and source mineralogy.
experiment: Published field characterization combining dune morphology, winds and sediment evidence.
limitations: Terrestrial sand flux and winds cannot be translated directly to Mars.

title: USGS characterization of Meteor Crater impact melts
research_objective: Characterize melt particle texture and composition to investigate impact mixing and shock processes.
selection_rationale: A well preserved simple impact crater and curated ejecta samples allow study of melting in sedimentary target material.
experiment: Scanning electron microscopy and electron microprobe analysis of curated particles.
limitations: Exact collection locations are unavailable for the dispersed particles.

title: Charyn terrestrial sedimentary archive
research_objective: Reconstruct Late Cenozoic moisture changes from an exposed sediment succession in the Ili Basin.
selection_rationale: The continuous sequence preserves alluvial, sheetwash and windblown deposition through changes in climate.
experiment: Field stratigraphy, chronology and isotope analysis of soil carbonates.
limitations: Terrestrial environmental evidence. The study did not certify a planetary analog.
